intro: Formulas, mnemonics and one-line shortcuts. What opens your head before you open the notebook.

items.f: sin = O/H · cos = A/H · tan = O/A
items.n: Sine: Opposite over Hypotenuse. Cosine: Adjacent over Hypotenuse. Tangent: Opposite over Adjacent.

items.f: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ
items.n: If you have sine and cosine, you never need anything else.
Moves you from one ratio to the other. Square root of one minus.
All, Sine, Tangent, Cosine — only the named one is positive.
Delta first, then the formula. Never the other way round.
Two roots, one root, none in the reals. Decide before you calculate.
Mental maths: two roots that sum and multiply right. Works with small numbers.
The midpoint of the two roots. Gives the max or min without differentiating.

items.f: m = (y₂ − y₁) / (x₂ − x₁) · y = mx + b
items.n: b is where it crosses the vertical axis. Perpendiculars: m₁ · m₂ = −1.

items.f: P(A and B) = P(A)·P(B) · P(A or B) = P(A)+P(B)
items.n: The word in the question names the operation. Circle the and and the or.
When it says at least one, count the none and subtract from 1.

items.f: mode = most often · median = middle · mean = sum/n
items.n: Sort first, always. The median is worthless in an unordered list.
Multiply across, divide by the one on top of the side that is missing.

items.f: a^m · a^n = a^(m+n)   (a^m)^n = a^(mn)   a^m / a^n = a^(m-n)
items.n: Same base: multiplying adds, a power of a power multiplies, dividing subtracts.
Look for the largest perfect square hiding inside the number.
A log is just the exponent you are hunting for. log(ab) = log a + log b.
Gauss: add the first to the last, multiply by half the terms.

items.f: A.P.: aₙ = a₁ + (n−1)r · G.P.: aₙ = a₁·qⁿ⁻¹
items.n: Arithmetic adds steps, geometric multiplies them. One less than n.
Right-angled triangles only. Memorise 3-4-5 and 5-12-13: they keep showing up.
Every triangle is half the rectangle around it. Memorise only one.
Area is squared, length is not. Pi only multiplies.
3.6 comes from 3600 s / 1000 m. Memorise the number, not the derivation.

items.f: v = Δs/Δt · v = v₀ + a·t · Δs = v₀t + a·t²/2
items.n: Three equations, five quantities: one is always missing, and that is the one you want.
No time in the question? Go straight here. v squared minus v-naught squared.
Stopping means final velocity zero. The sign of a sorts itself out if you pick an axis.

items.f: F = m·a · W = m·g · F_f = μ·N
items.n: Resultant force, not applied force. Draw the free-body diagram first, always.

items.f: Wₓ = W·sin θ · W_y = W·cos θ
items.n: The component that slides down is the sine one. Steeper slope, bigger sine, faster slide.

items.f: W = F·d·cos θ · KE = m·v²/2 · PE = m·g·h
items.n: Work needs displacement. Holding a suitcase is not work.
What you lose in height you gain in speed. Without friction the sum never changes.
Power is work in a hurry. Same force, more speed, more power.
In collisions and explosions, add the p before, set it equal to the p after. Heavier wins.
Force spread thin makes big pressure. In fluids only depth matters.
It pushes up by the weight of the fluid you displace. Whoever displaces more, floats.
Cover what you want in the V-I-R triangle. Power is always the product of the other two.
Series adds and grows. Parallel splits and shrinks — the total is smaller than the smallest.

items.f: series: same current · parallel: same voltage
items.n: Current does not split in series; voltage does not split in parallel.
Period and frequency are each other's reciprocal. Always.
ΔT is a change, not a temperature. Water needs a lot of c, metal needs little.
For magnetic force and solenoids. Settles the direction without memorising sign rules.
Convert everything to SI before calculating. The unit of the answer tells you if it is right.
